books.section: Topic 2.5 Interactions Between American Indians and Europeans
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.misconception: The Spanish were driven out; they did not choose to leave.
options.text: The Spanish voluntarily withdrew to concentrate on defending Florida.
Pueblo communities across many villages coordinated under Popé, striking simultaneously.

options.misconception: No French army invaded New Mexico in 1680.
options.text: French armies invaded New Mexico and defeated the Spanish garrisons there.

options.misconception: Epidemic disease devastated Native populations; it did not wipe out the missionaries.
options.text: A European epidemic wiped out the Spanish missionaries in New Mexico before the fighting even began.

rationales.A: The Spanish were driven out; they did not choose to leave.
rationales.B: The passage gives the answer in a single word: “coordinated.” Popé organized villages across New Mexico to rise at the same time, so the Spanish could not concentrate their forces or relieve the missions one by one. Scattered grievances became a single uprising — and a single uprising became an expulsion, because the Spanish were attacked everywhere at once, and no garrison could hold its ground alone.
rationales.C: No French army invaded New Mexico in 1680.
rationales.D: Epidemic disease devastated Native populations; it did not wipe out the missionaries.
rationales.general:
1. Find the passage's key word. Popé “coordinated” a rising across the Pueblos.
2. Ask what coordination does. It turns scattered grievances into a single uprising, everywhere at once.
3. Ask why the Spanish could not answer. They could not concentrate their forces or relieve the missions one by one.
Remember: the difference between a riot and a revolution is often planning.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Colin G. Calloway, New World for All (1997)
stem: Spain had held New Mexico since 1610 through its mission system. Which factor best explains why the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 succeeded in expelling the Spanish entirely instead of being quickly suppressed?

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Colin G. Calloway, New World for All (1997).
stimulus.text: In 1680, Popé, a Tewa religious leader from San Juan, coordinated a rising of the Pueblos that expelled the Spaniards for twelve years; rebels killed friars who had tried to crush their religion and destroyed Catholic ritual objects. When the Spanish returned, they had learned from the experience: where earlier friars had tried to wipe out every Native practice, they now often overlooked them. When Diego de Vargas campaigned to reconquer New Mexico in 1692, Luis, a Picuris leader, greeted him in animal skins with palm-shell headbands — but also wearing a rosary and carrying a silver cross. — paraphrased from Colin G. Calloway, New World for All (1997)
